facts.text: Tonasket takes its name from Chief Tonasket, a prominent Okanogan leader who rose to grand chief after the 1846 Oregon Treaty.
The town was officially incorporated on December 16, 1927, after being platted in 1910 and operating a post office since 1901.
Tonasket sits on the eastern bank of the Okanogan River, flanked by Siwash Creek to the north and Bonaparte Creek to the south.
Walter Brattain, a native of the area, shared the 1956 Nobel Prize for Physics for inventing the transistor while working at Bell Labs.
Every summer, the Okanogan Family Barter Faire brings thousands of visitors to trade handmade goods, vintage clothing, and local produce in Tonasket.
Tonasket experiences a dry-summer continental climate, with hot, dry summers and cold, snowy winters typical of north-central Washington.
